newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe seeks private investment in road network.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe seeks private investment in road network.

text.p: Zimbabwe Transport Minister Simon Moyo said on Wednesday his southern African country was opening up road development to private investors and invited U.S. businessmen to take the lead.

At a meeting on the sidelines of an African/African American business conference, he told U.S. Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater that President Robert Mugabe's cash-strapped government wanted to see Zimbabwe's major roads developed into dual carriageways.

"We would want the private sector to come in and our colleagues in the U.S. are very advanced in this area. They can come in and participate," Moyo said in remarks made in the presence of reporters after the closed-door meeting.
But Slater said the U.S. government and private investors would prefer participating in developing regional transport networks to help create a bigger trading market.
"In order to establish stronger trade, we need to get a good transportation system especially in the southern African region," he said.
Slater told Reuters on Tuesday he would work hard to convince cautious American investors to move into Africa, saying he would show concrete results within two years.
Slater and civil rights campaigner Jesse Jackson are President Bill Clinton's envoys to the four-day African/African American summit, which began on Tuesday.
The conference hopes to drum up trade, investment and economic aid for Africa, which has suffered slow economic growth.
